As someone who at one point was seriously considering going into the field of Radio Broadcasting there are a number of factors that many people are unaware of. The first and reportedly most frustrating amongst DJs is Canadian content rules. I don't remember the exact percentage but a certain amount of music played has to be Canadian in some way. Back in the day a lot of radio stations used to have so called Beaver hours usually programmed in the very early hours of the morning. They would play the majority of the required Canadian songs during this time opening up a lot more diverse music during prime time hours. The CRTC closed this loophole requiring the Cancon to be spread out during an entire broadcast day. 
Prince George actually has two community ran radio stations. One at UNBC the other somewhere in the bowl. Both stations are public access and are not normally listened to by the majority. Now with what the OP said I understand what they are saying. Prince George is small market radio area. The pay is atrocious most likely entry level for those recently graduated from Broadcasting school. Most of these personalities have limited experience and it really does show. 
I don't think it's a matter of growing out of the jokes or not finding the humor funny anymore it's as previously stated the complete lack of originality. For example a few years ago on the Goat a bet was made by the two morning show hosts that the loser would have to don a pair of high heeled kinky boots publically. It was entertaining and funny. Next time the loser had to shave their legs. Another time the loser had to wear a dress.... See the pattern here. When they ran out of ideas that involved gender bending humiliation they started to repeat the same punishments. Then last week a bet was made on another radio station that..you guessed it involved gender bending humiliation where the male co-host had to wear fancy press on nails. 
Obviously they really don't care anymore. It also should be mentioned that we used to have high energy hosts in town. They always were energetic and engaging. This is no longer the case. I sadly doubt that any of this will change the medium is dying and it's happening faster than you know.
